_about: The narration the voice reads, Scenario 2, draft 1 (S305, 2026-09-30), made from Scenario 1's v3 script (narration_s1.json, draft 4) for sheet 4 card 8: Sam, 2026-09-29, after the CO demo, "We're going with Scenario 2", college funding follows P1 and P2, and "I will be reporting on P3 Career Attainment together with P4 projects using more qualitative data rather than tying it to FTES." Eight scenes read word for word as Scenario 1's, because their figures are the same under the stored Scenario 2 config (read 2026-09-30, the model's own figures: $35,000,000; $25,240,308 to 118 institutions; Sample College's maximum $345,220 and its $340,861 credit and $4,358 noncredit shares). Two scenes differ: Two priorities (Access and Completion at half each, and the Chancellor's Office reporting career attainment with the innovation projects, card 7's reported cards) and Targets (Sample College's Access target, 67.2 FTES behind $170,431). The voice never names the scenario, which the picture carries, so the read survives the Chancellor's finalizing it. Spoken form, voice, fixes, bans and cues follow narration_s1.json; see its note. Not linked from the explainer: Scenario 2 waits on the Chancellor, and the cut on Sam's review.

scenes.text: Let's walk through how CPL Initiative funding works for twenty twenty-six through twenty-eight, and what it means for your college.

scenes.text: The state set aside thirty-five million dollars in one-time funding for the twenty-six, twenty-seven year. Just over twenty-five million of it goes straight to a hundred and eighteen institutions. The rest funds statewide CPL projects and technology, plus two Chancellor's Office positions that support colleges.

scenes.text: Every institution has a maximum allocation for the two years. It's based on the institution's share of instruction, credit and noncredit together, and it falls between a hundred and fifty thousand dollars and four hundred thousand. Sample College's maximum, for example, is about three hundred forty-five thousand.

scenes.text: That maximum splits into a credit share and a noncredit share, following each institution's own mix of instruction. And only noncredit outcomes count toward the noncredit share.

scenes.text: Two priorities carry the funding, in equal shares. Access counts applied CPL units from students who start at the CPL Portal, at your college's landing page, or through a batch upload. Completion counts transcribed CPL units, with the map counselor step checked. And the Chancellor's Office reports on career attainment together with the innovation projects, in qualitative terms.

cues.why: the heading, Two priorities carry the funding
the Access card, 50 percent
the Completion card, 50 percent
the reported card, Career attainment and innovation projects

scenes.text: Each priority has a target, measured in FTES. Thirty semester units of CPL make one FTES, or forty-five if you're on the quarter system. Sample College's Access target, for example, is about sixty-seven FTES, behind about a hundred seventy thousand dollars. Here's the part to remember: reach half of a target, and your college qualifies for half that share. Go past the target, and the share stays where it is. It's the ceiling.

scenes.text: Before any funding is released, your college meets three minimum conditions by November first. Name a CPL coordinator, then list that person in map and on your college's CPL landing page. Put your local confirmation of participation on file. And make sure at least seventy-five percent of your enrolled veterans have their Joint Services Transcripts uploaded in map. Until all three are met, the funding your college demonstrates is held in reserve for it.

scenes.text: The Chancellor's Office releases funding twice a year, based on your college's CPL to date. The full two-year amount is available from year one, and whatever remains after year one carries forward to year two for your college.
